examInfo.format: Multiple choice assessment taken after the ServSafe Food Handler course. The official assessment has 40 questions, is not proctored, and has no time limit. This practice mock uses 40 questions with 4 answer choices and a 60-minute timer so you can practice at a steady pace. Some states and local areas use their own versions (for example, California), and they may differ.

passCriteria.description: ServSafe says you need a score of at least 75% to receive the Food Handler Certificate of Achievement. On a 40-question test, that means at least 30 correct answers. Some state or local versions use a different passing score, so check your course.

content.eligibility: Anyone can take the ServSafe Food Handler course and assessment. There are no education or work requirements. Many states, counties, and employers require food workers to hold a food handler certificate, so check what your health department or employer accepts.
content.intro: The ServSafe Food Handler assessment checks the basic food safety knowledge every food worker needs. The course has five sections: Basic Food Safety, Personal Hygiene, Cross-contamination and Allergens, Time and Temperature, and Cleaning and Sanitation. After the course, you take a 40-question assessment. A score of 75% or higher earns the ServSafe Food Handler Certificate of Achievement.
content.trendSummary: Questions focus on everyday kitchen tasks and the numbers behind them: the temperature danger zone (41°F to 135°F), minimum cooking temperatures, safe cooling and reheating, how to wash hands, when to change gloves, which illnesses to report, how to store food to prevent cross-contamination, the major food allergens, and how to clean and sanitize. The temperatures and times on this site follow the U.S. FDA Food Code. The chapters on this site follow the five course sections, but the weights are study estimates, not official numbers.
content.studyTip: Start with Time and Temperature, because many questions use its numbers. Make one card with every temperature and time (41°F, 135°F, 165°F, 155°F, 145°F, 2 hours, 6 hours, 20 seconds) and review it daily. Then practice the order of handwashing and the order for storing food in the refrigerator. Before you take the real assessment, take a full 40-question mock and aim for 34 or more.

faqs.question: How many questions are on the ServSafe Food Handler assessment?
faqs.answer: ServSafe describes the standard assessment as 40 questions. It is not proctored and has no time limit. State versions may differ.

faqs.question: What score do I need to pass?
faqs.answer: ServSafe says you need at least 75% to receive the Certificate of Achievement. That is 30 of 40 questions. Some state or local versions use a different passing score.

faqs.question: Is this the same as the ServSafe Manager exam?
faqs.answer: No. The Manager exam is a longer, proctored certification exam for managers. This page is only for the Food Handler assessment.

faqs.question: Are these real test questions?
faqs.answer: No. Every question on this site is an original practice question written with AI from the public course outline and the FDA Food Code. ServSafe does not publish its assessment questions.

studyTips.studyOrder: Start with Time and Temperature, the biggest chapter on this site, because its numbers show up across the whole test. Then study Personal Hygiene and Cross-contamination and Allergens, which cover what you do with your hands and food every shift. Finish with Basic Food Safety and Cleaning and Sanitation, and then take a full 40-question mock.
studyTips.hardChapters: Time and Temperature is where most numbers are: the 41°F to 135°F danger zone, cooking temperatures of 165°F, 155°F, and 145°F, and the two-stage cooling rule (2 hours to 70°F, then 4 more hours to 41°F). In Cross-contamination and Allergens, practice the refrigerator storage order from top to bottom. In Personal Hygiene, learn the handwashing steps in order and which symptoms you must report.
studyTips.examDay: The official assessment has 40 questions and no time limit, so read each question fully and do not rush. You need 75%, which is 30 correct answers, so you can miss up to 10. If two answers look right, pick the one that keeps food safest, such as the colder holding temperature or the more frequent handwashing.
